question.problem:
Given that
$M=[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $M=LU,$ then $L=$
question.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $M$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $M$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{5}){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot M \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(\frac{3}{2}){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot M \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}M=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}M & =U \\ {E}_{1}M & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ M & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ M & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ M & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ M & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$
